header.name: Acuña Lab
header.tagline: To reveal how the body heals the brain's pain, and turn that knowledge into therapies anyone can access.
header.description:
We study the neural mechanisms underlying chronic pain and exercise-induced analgesia, investigating both peripheral and central pathways that modulate pain perception. Our work bridges body and brain using in vivo calcium imaging, electrophysiology, and molecular profiling.

We are part of the Nevian Lab at the Institute of Physiology, University of Bern.

projects.title: Body to Brain — Deciphering the Role of Myokines in Pain Modulation and Brain Activity
projects.description:
This project investigates how exercise alleviates pain by examining the relationship between physical activity, myokine production, and brain activity. Using various exercise paradigms and chronic pain models, we study how specific myokines contribute to pain modulation and analyze the associated neuronal dynamics in the medial prefrontal cortex. Through a combination of behavioral assays, molecular profiling, and advanced neuroimaging, we aim to uncover the peripheral mechanisms that drive exercise-induced analgesia.
Carried out by Alessandro Arcari

projects.title: Brain to Body — Unraveling the Neuronal Mechanisms Implicated in Exercise-Mediated Analgesia
projects.description:
This project focuses on the central neural circuits involved in exercise-induced pain relief, particularly the ventral hippocampus-medial prefrontal cortex-periaqueductal gray (vHC-mPFC-PAG) axis. Through comprehensive circuit mapping and selective manipulation of neuronal populations, we investigate how this pathway contributes to pain modulation during exercise. By combining circuit-specific interventions with targeted myokine overexpression, we seek to understand and potentially enhance the pain-relieving effects of exercise, developing novel approaches for those unable to engage in regular physical activity.
Carried out by Sascha Steiner

join.title: Join Us
join.content:
We are looking for motivated Master students to join our lab. If you are curious about the neuroscience of pain and exercise, this is the place for you.

What you will learn:
• Molecular biology (qPCR, immunohistochemistry)
• Ex vivo electrophysiology
• Data analysis

How to apply:
Send an email to mario[dot]acuna[at]unibe[dot]ch with your CV and two sentences on why pain and exercise interest you. No cover letter needed — just curiosity and motivation.
